translation: Dhritarashtra said: O Sanjaya, what did my sons and Pandu's sons do, assembled in Kurukshetra, the land of Dharma?
Sanjayu Palikenu: Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava army stationed in military strategy, approached his teacher Dronacharya and said this.
Duryodhana spoke:  Respected Guruvarya! Behold this great army of Pandavas, most strategically held by your dear disciple, the son of Drupada.

Look at the many mighty warriors in the army on their side - like Yuudhana, Virata and Drupada who wear great bows and are equal to Bhimarjuna. There were the mighty Dhrishtaketa, Chekita, the heroic Kasiraja, Purujittu, Kuntibhoja and Saibya - all of them the best of men. As in their army - the brave Yudhamanya, the heroic Uttamauja, the son of Subhadra, the sons of Draupadi - all these were warriors.

Look at the many mighty warriors in the army on their side - like Yuudhana, Virata and Drupada who wear great bows and are equal to Bhimarjuna. There were the mighty Dhrishtaketa, Chekita, the heroic Kasiraja, Purujittu, Kuntibhoja and Saibya - all of them the best of men. As in their army - the brave Yudhamanya, the heroic Uttamauja, the son of Subhadra, the sons of Draupadi - all these were warriors.

Look at the many mighty warriors in the army on their side - like Yuudhana, Virata and Drupada who wear great bows and are equal to Bhimarjuna. There were the mighty Dhrishtaketa, Chekita, the heroic Kasiraja, Purujittu, Kuntibhoja and Saibya - all of them the best of men. As in their army - the brave Yudhamanya, the heroic Uttamauja, the son of Subhadra, the sons of Draupadi - all these were warriors.
O Brahmin, hear also of the chief warriors on our side, who are most worthy of leaders. I am telling you about them now for your interest.
You, Bhishma, Karna, Kripacharya, Ashwatthama, Vikarna and Bhurishrava - all of them are ever victorious in battle.
Many more warriors are ready to lay down their lives for me. Armed with many weapons, all of them are proficient in martial arts.
Our military strength is unlimited and we are protected by father Bhishma, but the Pandava army protected by Bhima is limited.
Therefore, I call upon all Kaurava Sena leaders to protect your strategic positions and render full cooperation to Bhishma Pitamahu.
Then Bhishma, the great progenitor of the Kuru clan, roared like a lion and filled his conch with a loud noise; This made Duryodhana happy.
After that conches, drums, tambourines, bheris and horn instruments sounded at once, the sound of all of them together was terrifying.
Then, from the midst of the Pandava army, seated in a splendid chariot full of white horses, Madhava and Arjuna filled their divine conchshells.
Hrishikesh filled the conch known as 'Panchajanyam'. Arjuna fills Devadatta. A great eater and a doer of the most difficult tasks, Bhima filled a gigantic conch called 'Poundram'.

Oh ruler of the earth! Maharaja Yudhishthira completed Anantavijaya. Nakula Sahadeva, Sughosha filled the manipushpakams. The five sons of the great archer King Kasi, the charioteer Sikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, the invincible Satyaki, Drupada, and Draupadi; Strong-armed, Abhimanyu, the son of Subhadra, all filled their conch shells.

O Dhritarashtra, the earth and heavens trembled at that terrible sound; It broke the hearts of your sons.
At that time, Arjuna, the son of Pandu, who had the symbol of Hanuman on his chariot flag, took his bow. Seeing your sons standing in front of Samara, O king, Arjuna said to Sri Krishna.
Arjuna said this. Achyuta (Sri Krishna), please stop my chariot between the two armies. In this great struggle, I must test who is standing on the battlefield and who is to fight.
Arjuna said this. Achyuta (Sri Krishna), please stop my chariot between the two armies. In this great struggle, I must test who is standing on the battlefield and who is to fight.
I want to see all those who have come to war on his side to please the mischievous Dhritarashtra's son.
Sanjaya said: O Dhritarashtra, thus, as requested by Arjuna, conqueror of sleep, Sri Krishna drove that glorious chariot between the two armies.
In the presence of Bhishma, Dronacharya and other kings, Lord Krishna said, "O Partha, see the Kurus clan gathered here".
There Arjuna saw his fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, cousins, sons, grandsons, friends, uncles and well-wishers who were in both armies.
Arjuna, the son of Kunti, seeing all his relatives there, filled with compassion, uttered this in great sorrow.
Arjuna said: O Krishna, seeing my relatives ready for battle and trying to kill each other, my limbs fail and my mouth dries up.

My whole body was shaking; Hair is getting thick.  My bow, the gandivam, slips away and all my skin is missing. My mind is wandering in a state of confusion. I can't hold myself steady anymore. O Krishna, slayer of the demon Kesi (Kesavah), there are ominous omens everywhere. Killing one's own kinsmen in this war, I fail to see how any good can come of it.

O Krishna, slayer of the demon Kesi (Kesavah), there are ominous omens everywhere. Killing one's own kinsmen in this war, I fail to see how any good can come of it.

O Krishna, I do not want victory, kingdom, or the happiness that comes from them. What is the use of the kingdom, of the pleasures, of this life, when those for whom we want all this are fighting against us?

O Krishna, I do not want victory, kingdom, or the happiness that comes from them. What is the use of the kingdom, of the pleasures, of this life, when those for whom we want all this are fighting against us?

Gurus, fathers, sons, uncles, grandsons, uncles, brothers-in-law and other relatives risk their lives and money and come here.  O Madhusudana, even if they attack me I will not kill them. If we kill the sons of Dhritarashtra and gain dominion over the mountains, what satisfaction will we have, and what will I say for the sake of this earth?

Gurus, fathers, sons, uncles, grandsons, uncles, brothers-in-law and other relatives risk their lives and money and come here.  O Madhusudana, even if they attack me I will not kill them. If we kill the sons of Dhritarashtra and gain dominion over the mountains, what satisfaction will we have, and what will I say for the sake of this earth?

O Janardhana (protector and patron of all demons), how can we be happy after killing the sons of Dhritarashtra? Even if they are evil aggressors, if we kill them, we will surely be covered with sin. So it is not proper for us to kill Dhritarashtra's sons and friends. O Madhva (Krishna), how can we be happy by killing our own?

O Janardhana (protector and patron of all demons), how can we be happy after killing the sons of Dhritarashtra? Even if they are evil aggressors, if we kill them, we will surely be covered with sin. So it is not proper for us to kill Dhritarashtra's sons and friends. O Madhva (Krishna), how can we be happy by killing our own?

They see no fault in greed corrupting their thoughts and destroying their relatives, or in betraying their friends by taking sides. But, O Janardhana, why should not we, who can clearly see the error in killing ourselves, avoid this sinful act?

They see no fault in greed corrupting their thoughts and destroying their relatives, or in betraying their friends by taking sides. But, O Janardhana, why should not we, who can clearly see the error in killing ourselves, avoid this sinful act?
When the lineage is destroyed, all lineages disappear; The rest of the family members are unrighteous.
Due to the predominance of vices, O Krishna, caste women become unrighteous, and due to the immoral conduct of women, O Vrishni, unwanted offspring are born.
Due to the increase of unwanted children, the caste and also those who destroyed the caste will be in hell. Even those depraved lineage ancestors will fall because of Shraddha tarpanams.
Many social and family welfare virtues are destroyed due to their evil deeds which destroy the family tradition and cause unwanted children.
O Janardhana (Krishna), I have heard from the scholars that those who destroy castes will remain in hell indefinitely;

Oops! What a surprise, we decided to commit this great sin. We are ready to kill our own relatives for the pleasures of the kingdom. Even if the sons of Dhritarashtra, armed with weapons, slay me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield, better than this.

Oops! What a surprise, we decided to commit this great sin. We are ready to kill our own relatives for the pleasures of the kingdom. Even if the sons of Dhritarashtra, armed with weapons, slay me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield, better than this.
Sanjaya uttered: Thus uttered Arjuna, in a state of dejection, deeply grieved, threw aside his arrows and bow, and collapsed in the chariot.
Sanjaya spoke: Seeing Arjuna full of pity, with a sorrowful heart and eyes full of water, Lord Krishna spoke thus.

Sri Bhagavan said: Dear Arjuna, at such a critical time, how did this illusion of mind hide itself? This is unbecoming of a respectable person. This does not lead to the best results, but it can lead to scandal.
O Partha, it is not fit for you to surrender to this cowardly self. Abandon this wretched weakness of heart, and go forth to battle, O conqueror of foes.
Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, how can I shoot arrows in battle against the venerable Bhishma and Dronacharya? O destroyer of enemies.
It is better to live as a beggar than to kill these elders who are my teachers and enjoy these pleasures. If we kill them, our wealth, pleasures, and blood will be tainted.

We do not even know which outcome of this war is better for us - to conquer them or to be conquered by them. Even after killing them we don't feel like living. However, they joined the side of Dhritarashtra and stood in front of us on the battlefield.
I did not know what my duty was and anxiety and timidity seized me. I am your disciple and your devotee. Teach me what is really good for me.
There is no way to get rid of this grief that dries up my senses. Even if I win an opulent, unrivaled kingdom on this earth and rule like the gods, I cannot remove this sorrow.
Sanjaya spoke: thus Gudakesha, the chastiser of enemies, fell silent, saying to Hrishikesh: "Govinda, I will not fight."
O Dhritarashtra! After that, in the midst of the two armies, Lord Krishna spoke to the grieving Arjuna.
The Lord said: You speak words of wisdom but mourn for that which should not be mourned.  The wise mourn neither the dead nor the living.
There was no time when I, but you, and all these kings were not; We will not be absent even before.

However, just as the soul in the body passes through childhood, youth and old age respectively, similarly at the time of death, the soul enters another body (body). Wise people do not worry about this.

O son of Kunti, due to association with sense-objects, the senses seem to have fleeting, eternal pleasures and sorrows. These are infinities; They come like summer and winter. O descendant of Bharata, learn to bear these things without getting upset.
O Arjuna, the best of men, he who is unaffected by pleasures and sorrows, and is unmoved by both, is worthy of salvation.
That which is transitory has no permanence and that which is eternal has no end. Philosophers who have studied the nature of these two have observed this fact.
Know that it is indestructible which pervades the whole body. No one can destroy the impermanent soul.
Only this physical body is perishable; But the Jivatma is imperishable, immeasurable and Sanatana (Eternal). Therefore, O descendant of Bharata, fight.
He who thinks that the soul kills others and he who thinks that the soul is killed by others are both ignorant. Indeed the soul does not kill anyone, nor is it killed by anyone.
The soul has no birth and never dies. Once was and will never cease to be. Atman is birthless, eternal, eternal and ageless. When the body perishes it does not perish.
O Partha, who knows that the soul is indestructible, eternal, without birth and death, how can he kill (anyone)? How can he be the cause of death?
Just as a human being discards his worn-out old clothes and puts on new clothes, so the soul at the time of death leaves the old body and assumes a new body.
This soul, weapons cannot break, fire cannot burn, water cannot destroy, wind cannot destroy.
Spirit, unbroken and unburnt; It cannot be wetted (by water), nor can it be dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, immutable, immutable and eternal.
Atman is immanent (unseen), unimaginable and immutable. Knowing this you should not grieve for the body.
But even if you think that the soul undergoes repeated births and deaths, O great-armed one, you should not mourn like this.
One who is born is bound to die, and one who dies is bound to be reborn. So do not grieve for this inevitable thing.
O descendant of Bharata, all created beings are unmanifest before birth, unmanifest during life, and unmanifest after death. So why mourn?
Some see this spirit as wonderful, some describe it as wonderful, some hear that the spirit is wonderful, and others, even after hearing, do not understand anything about it.
O Arjuna, the soul within the body is immortal; So you should not mourn for any creature.
Further, following your Kshatriya sva-dharmam you should not waver. In fact, a Kshatriya has no other duty than to fight for the preservation of Dharma.
O Partha, the Kshatriyas are fortunate, given the opportunity to preserve the Dharma without seeking it. It is an open door to heaven for them.
But if you leave your self-righteousness and glory and refuse to fight this righteous war, you will surely become a sinner.
People call you a coward and a deserter. To an honorable man dishonor is worse than death.
Great are you in the eyes of the great charioteers, who, fearing you, flee from the battlefield. You will lose their respect for you.
Your enemies will slander you and insult you with cruel words, thereby diminishing your greatness. Ugh, is there anything more painful than this?
If you fight, you will die a heroic death on the battlefield and go to heaven, or you will enjoy this kingdom as a victor. Therefore, be determined, O son of Kunti, and prepare for battle.
Take the joys and sorrows, profit and loss equally - fight as duty. By performing your duties in this way you will never feel guilty.

So far I have explained to you Sankhya Yoga, i.e., the analytical knowledge of Atma Tattva. Now listen, O Partha, I will explain Buddhi Yoga. When you act with this awareness you will be freed from karmic bonds.
When working with this perspective, there is no harm but opposite results. Even a little practice can save us from big dangers.
O descendant of Kuru, those on this path are steadfast in their minds, their goal is one. But, the mind of those who are not fixed will be in the way of surroundings.

Those of limited understanding are attracted by the seductive words of the Vedas, which refer to pretentious rituals for the attainment of the heavenly world, and think that there is nothing higher in it. They glorify those parts of the Vedas that bring them sensual pleasures and perform extravagant rituals for higher birth, wealth, sensual pleasures, access to the heavenly world, etc.

Those of limited understanding are attracted by the seductive words of the Vedas, which refer to pretentious rituals for the attainment of the heavenly world, and think that there is nothing higher in it. They glorify those parts of the Vedas that bring them sensual pleasures and perform extravagant rituals for higher birth, wealth, sensual pleasures, access to the heavenly world, etc.
With much attachment to worldly pleasures and pleasures, their minds become delusional and they cannot have the firm will required for success in the path of Bhagavadprapti.

Arjuna, the Vedas explain the three-fold subjectivity of physical nature. Be thou in a state of pure spiritual knowledge beyond these trigunas. Detach from dualities, be eternally established in the Supreme Truth, and remain steadfast in the sense of self, regardless of material gains and security.
All the advantages of a small water well can naturally be obtained with a large pool of water. In this way he who knows the supreme truth and attains Bhagavat attains the goal of all the Vedas.

You have the authority to perform the ritual duty prescribed by Shastra, but you have no right over the fruits of that karma.  Never think that you are the reason for the fruits of karma and do not be interested in doing the karmas that should be done.
Be steadfast in the performance of your duty, O Arjuna. Such equanimity is called yoga.

Take refuge in divine spiritual knowledge. O Arjuna, give up fruitive actions; They are of a lower order than those which keep the mind fixed in spiritual divine knowledge. Those who want to enjoy the fruits of their karma are greedy/hungry.
One who wisely practices this Karma Shastra will renounce both the virtues and sins in this very birth. So practice yoga, which means working with skill (with right attitude).

The wise, possessing equanimity, have renounced mamkara-interests in the fruits of karma that bind them in the cycle of birth and death. By working with such a feeling, one attains a state of sorrowlessness.
Only when your mind is freed from the quicksand of passion, do you feel disillusioned with what you have heard so far and what you are going to hear. (In the case of pleasures of this world).
When your mind is fixed on God instead of being attracted to the Vedic sections that tell the stems of Kamya Karma, then you will attain the state of complete yoga.
Arjuna said: O Kesava, what is the disposition of one who is steady (sthitaprajna) of Bhagavat dhyasa nande?  How does an enlightened person speak? How does he sit? How does he walk?
Lord Palikenu said: O Partha, when one is satisfied in the knowledge of the Self, abandoning all selfish interests and sensual desires that torment the mind, that person is called Stitha Prajna.
He who is not disturbed even in the midst of sorrows, who is born for pleasures; One who has given up anger, fear and anger is called a wise sage.
He who is disinterested in all situations, does not rejoice in good fortune and is not depressed by hardships, is a sage of perfect knowledge.
He who can withdraw the senses from their objects, as a tortoise withdraws its limbs into its shell, is fixed in divine spiritual knowledge.
Even if the Sadhaka controls the senses from the objects of pleasure, the taste remains for the objects of the senses. But, when you understand the philosophy of Bhagwat, that taste also ends.
The senses are so forceful and turbulent that they can forcibly seize the mind of even a wise and self-controlled sadhaka, O son of Kunti.
Those who keep their senses under control and always fix their mind on Me, they are in perfect knowledge.
Dwelling on sense objects increases lust for them. This interest gives rise to desires, and from those desires arises anger.
Anger leads to indiscretion, which causes illusory memory. When there is amnesia, the mind perishes. When the mind perishes, man falls.
One who controls the mind and is free from mamkara-dwesha even while using sense objects/objects is eligible for the grace of God.
By Bhagwat's grace one gets the supreme peace in which all sorrows are removed. Thus the intellect of one with a happy mind is quick and fixed in God.

One who is undisciplined and does not control the mind and senses, there is no stable intellect, no steady meditation of Bhagavat. He who never unites his mind with God has no peace. How can one who lacks peace of mind be happy?
Just as a strong wind pushes a boat off its course in water, it drains the mind if the mind is concentrated on any one sense.
Therefore, O Arjuna, one with mighty arms, one who has completely restrained the senses from the senses, is steadfast in spiritual knowledge.
What is day for all demons is the night of ignorance for the scholar, and what is night for all demons is day for the introverted sage.

Even though many rivers are eternally converging within him, as the ocean is still/tranquil, similarly many desirable objects keep coming around him, the unmoved Yogi attains peace; A person who strives to satisfy desires does not get it.
One who renounces all worldly desires, without greed, without sense of I/mine, without ego, such a person attains perfect tranquility.

O Partha, what is the state of an enlightened soul, once enlightened it never again falls into delusion.  Even at the time of death, such a person who is steadfast in this wisdom, is freed from the cycle of birth and death and reaches the divine abode of that Lord.

Arjuna said: O Janardhana, if knowledge is better than karma, then why do you want me to fight this terrible battle? My mind was bewildered by your vague instruction. Kindly instruct me that one way which will bring me the best prosperity.

Arjuna said: O Janardhana, if knowledge is better than karma, then why do you want me to fight this terrible battle? My mind was bewildered by your vague instruction. Kindly instruct me that one way which will bring me the best prosperity.

The Lord thus spoke: O sinless one, there are two paths to Bhagavat-prapti (enlightenment) which have been told by me earlier: the path of knowledge for those interested in meditative devotion; Karma Marga for those interested in work.
Man cannot be freed from karmic bondage (pratikriya) without performing karmas. Also, only through external (physical) asceticism one attains Jnana Siddhi.
No one can stop practicing karma even for a single moment. In fact, all living beings are motivated by their inherent nature (tri-gunas) to perform karma.
Those who keep their external senses under control, but think only about the things of the senses in their minds, are self-deluders, and such people are called hypocrites.
But, Arjuna, the Karma Yogis who control their sense organs with the mind and work without mamkara/interests with the Karmandriyas, are truly excellent.

So you should perform the prescribed duty in accordance with the Vedas, because doing things is better than inaction (abiding).  Even maintenance of the body is not possible due to leaving out activities.

Works should be done like a yajna, an offering to Bhagavat, or else those works will tie us in karmic bonds in this world.  Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform the duties assigned to you, without interest in their results, for the satisfaction of God.
At the beginning of creation, Lord Brahma, who created mankind along with their duties, said, "Prosper by performing these yajnas. These fulfill all your desires."
Gods will be pleased by your yajnas. The mutual cooperation of Gods and humans brings prosperity to all.

The deities, who are satisfied with the performance of yajnas, bestow all that is necessary for the maintenance of life. Those who enjoy what is given to them, without reporting it back to the gods, are thieves indeed.
The spiritual minded good men who eat only the rest of the food reported first in the Yajna will be freed from all sins. Those who cook rice for their own pleasure eat sin.
All living things live on food and food is produced by rains. By performing yajnas rain falls and by performing prescribed duties (vihita karmas) yajna is born.

The prescribed karmas (duties) of human beings are enunciated in the Vedas, and the Vedas are revealed from the Lord Himself.  Therefore, the all-pervading Lord is always present in the yajna activities.
Those who do not fulfill their obligation in this yajna cycle prescribed by the Vedas are sinners. They live only for their sensual pleasures; So their life is wasted.
But those who are happy in the soul, with perfect knowledge and contented in the soul, have no duty.
Such enlightened souls have nothing to gain or lose (gains and losses) from doing or not doing their duties (karmas).  There is no need for them to depend on other beings for their selfish benefit.
So, abandon the bonds of mamkara, be disinterested and perform your tasks as a duty.  By working without interest in the fruits of karma, a human being can reach that Supreme Self.

By performing their dharmas (prescriptive actions), people like Janaka Maharaja attained siddhi. You should also do your duty to set a good example to the world. Common people imitate what the great do. The standard they set is followed by the whole world.

By performing their dharmas (prescriptive actions), people like Janaka Maharaja attained siddhi. You should also do your duty to set a good example to the world. Common people imitate what the great do. The standard they set is followed by the whole world.
In these three worlds I have nothing to do, Arjuna, nothing to gain, nothing to achieve. But I will continue to do my duties.
If I do not carefully perform my prescribed actions, O Partha, all men will follow my path in every way.
If I do not perform my duties, all these worlds will be destroyed. I will be responsible for the chaos that will happen, and the human race will be without peace.
Just as the ignorant perform their duties with interest in the fruits of karma, O Bharata Vamsiya, the wise should also perform their karmas (for the sake of lokahit), to guide the people aright.

The wise should not delude the mind of the ignorant, who perform the karmas with falsakti, by encouraging them not to perform the karmas. Moreover, performing their duties in a state of enlightenment, they should also inspire the ignorant to perform prescribed rituals.
All actions are done by the trigunas of nature. But, in ignorance, the soul, thinking that it is this body, thinks that it is the Karta (doer).

O great-armed Arjuna, the wise see the soul as separate from the qualities and karma. Knowing that the gunas (in the form of the senses, the mind) are moving in the gunas (in the material form of sense perception) they are not interested in them.
Those who are deluded by the tendency of qualities, are interested in the fruits of their karma. But the wise who understand these truths should not disturb the ignorant.
Do all activities as a sacrifice to Me and keep your meditation on Me, the Supreme Lord.  Abandoning hope, self-concern, and mental grief, fight!
Those who follow this teaching of mine with full attention, faith, without questioning, will be freed from karmic bonds.
But, those who find faults in this teaching of mine, lack knowledge and discernment, neglect these doctrines and seek their own depravity.
Wise people also do things according to their nature. All living beings act according to their natural instincts. What is the point of restraining it?
The senses naturally have raga aversions to sense objects, but should not be subdued by them, as these are obstacles and enemies to us.

It is better to practice one's natural dharma, even if it is flawed, than to do the dharma of others well. In fact, it is good to die in the practice of self-righteousness, but to follow the path of others (doing other dharma) is dangerous.
Arjuna said: O Vrishni Vamsiya (Sri Krishna), why is a person induced to do sinful deeds, even if unwillingly, as if taken by some force?
Sri Bhagavanu Palikenu: It is Kama (desires, longings) arising from Rajo guna, which further evolves into anger. Know it as the sin that destroys the world.
As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror is dimmed by dust, as an unborn child is enfolded by pregnancy - one's knowledge is consumed by lust (desire).
Even the wisdom of the wisest is overshadowed by the enemy in the form of desire, which is never satisfied and burns like fire, O son of Kunti.
Senses, mind, intellect - these are said to be the seat of desires. By them it obscures the knowledge of the individual and deludes the living soul.
Therefore, O great Bharata, exterminate this supremely sinful enemy, kama (desires), which in the first place brings the senses under control and destroys the knowledge.
The senses are superior to the gross body, and the mind is superior to the senses. Higher than the mind is the intellect and higher than the intellect is the soul.
Thus knowing that the soul is superior to the material intellect, O great-armed one, you (the senses), subdue (by the power of the soul), and slay the mighty enemy of lust.
Sri Krishna Paramatma said: I told this orthodox Yoga Shastra to Surya Bhagavan Vivasvan. He taught this to Manu and Manu to Ikshvaku.
O vanquisher of enemies, the kings thus obtained the science of Yoga in succession. But in course of time it has disappeared (decayed) in this world.
I am imparting to you today the same ancient supreme secret, this science of yoga. Because you are my friend and devotee, who can understand this transcendental knowledge.
Arjuna said: You were born in what period after Vivasvana. And thou hast taught him this education in the beginning, how should I understand it?
Sri Bhagavan said: Both of us have passed many births. O Arjuna, thou hast forgotten them, but I remember them all, O Parantapa.
Even though I am birthless, even though I am the Lord of all beings, and even though I am imperishable, I appear in this world by my divine power, Yogamaya.
Whenever dharma declines or unrighteousness prevails, O Arjuna, at that time I create myself in the earth.
I will incarnate in this world in every age to protect the righteous, exterminate the wicked, and re-establish the principles of righteousness.
Whoever understands the divine nature of my birth and deeds, O Arjuna, they will not be born again after leaving their body, but will come to my eternal abode.
Being free from anger-hate-anger, fully established in Me, many who have taken refuge in Me have been purified by My wisdom before and thus obtained My divine love.
As men submit to Me, so will I respond to them. Knowing or not, all must follow my path, O Arjuna.
Those who are desirous of success in material (worldly) karmas in this world worship the deities, because material rewards are quick.
Based on the qualities and activities of people, four types of Vrittis Dharma have been created by Me. Even though I am the creator of this system, know Me as Akarta and Sanatana.
Karmas do not speak to me, I am not interested in the fruits of karma either. Those who know Me in this way will not be entangled in karmic bonds.
Knowing this truth, those who sought salvation in ancient times also practiced their karmas. So, walking in the footsteps of the ancients, you too do your duty.
What is Karma? What is Akarma? Even the wise are at a loss to understand this. Now I will explain to you the secret of karma, by knowing which, you can free yourself from material bonds.
Karma, Vikarma, Akarma – you must know the nature of these three – the truth about these is mysterious and difficult to understand.
He who sees karma in akarma and akarma in karma is the true sage among human beings. They are yogis and do all their karmas, even if they continue to do all the karmas.
Those whose all karmas are beyond the desires of material pleasures and who have burnt all their karmic tribulations in the fire of knowledge are called, by the enlightened Munas, Pandits.
Such people, who have renounced interest/attachment to their karmic fruits, are always contented and do not depend on external material things. Whatever they do, even if they are engaged in karmas.
One who is despondent, without feeling that nothing is mine, and whose mind is under full control of his senses, does not incur any sin, even if he continues to do karma with his body.

Content with whatever comes naturally, free from jealousy, and unaffected by dualities such as pleasure and pain, success and failure—they perform all duties with equanimity and remain unbound by karmic consequences.
Such are freed from worldly attachments and their mind is fixed in divine spiritual knowledge. Everything they do is Yajna (offering to Bhagavat) so they are freed from all kinds of karmic reaction.

For those who are in full Bhagavat Dhyasa, the Homa dravya is Brahman, the stream used to offer it in Yajna is Brahman, the ritual of Yajna is Brahman, and the Yajna fire is also Brahman. Those who see everything as God will attain God easily.
Some yogis worship the deities by offering material objects. Some others worship completely by offering their souls in the fire of supreme truth.
Others offer sravana and other senses in a yagna called indriyanigrahana. Others offer sound and other sense objects as burnt in the fire of sense.
Some, inspired by wisdom, surrender all their sense activities, and even their life force, in the fire of the restrained mind.

Some offer their wealth as a yajna, while others offer strict devotions as a yajna. Some practice the eightfold yoga practice, while others practice strict austerities and study the Vedic scriptures as a yajna to gain knowledge.

Others offer the in-breath as a sacrifice of the out-breath; Someone else submits the in-breath to the out-breath. Some are engaged in the control of Prana Shakti and practice Pranayama with devotion to control the incoming and outgoing breaths. Still others, with reduced food, offer the breath as a sacrifice to the Prana Shakti. All those who know such a yajna are purified from their impurities by such processes.

Others offer the in-breath as a sacrifice of the out-breath; Someone else submits the in-breath to the out-breath. Some are engaged in the control of Prana Shakti and practice Pranayama with devotion to control the incoming and outgoing breaths. Still others, with reduced food, offer the breath as a sacrifice to the Prana Shakti. All those who know such a yajna are purified from their impurities by such processes.

Those who know the secret of Yajna, perform it, receive its immortal essence, and progress towards the Supreme Truth. O noble one of the Kuru clan, those who do not perform any kind of yajna, will not get any happiness either in this world or in the next.
All these different types of Yajnas are described in the Vedas. Know that they are derived from different types of work. It is this knowledge that negates your physical entanglement.
O conqueror of enemies, how much better is a yajna done with knowledge than a yajna done mechanically with money. However, O Partha, all yajna karmas end in knowledge.
Join a spiritual master and learn the ultimate truth. Humbly ask Him questions and serve Him. Such a great sage can enlighten you because he himself has seen the truth.

Following this path and enlightened by the Guru, O Arjuna, you will never again fall into lust. With this illumination of knowledge, you will realize that all living beings are parts (amsa) of God, that they reside in Me.
Even those who are considered to be the most sinful of all sinners can cross this worldly space by staying in the boat of spiritual divine knowledge.
As a blazing fire consumes firewood, so, O Arjuna, the fire of knowledge consumes all miseries arising from material actions.

There is nothing else in this world that the Pavitramoner can do better than divine spiritual knowledge. After attaining Antahkarana Shuddhi with long yoga practice, this knowledge is acquired in the heart of the practitioner in the order of time.
Those who have deep devotion and practice controlling their senses acquire divine spiritual knowledge. With such excellent transcendental knowledge they quickly attain eternal supreme peace.
Those who lack knowledge and faith and have a doubting nature will fall away. Those who have no faith and doubt will have no happiness in this world or in the Hereafter.
O Arjuna, those who have renounced karma in the fire of yoga, have all their doubts cleared by knowledge, and who are in the knowledge of the self, are not bound by karma.
So, with the sword of knowledge, cut the doubts in your heart. O descendant of Bharata, be steadfast in Karma Yoga. Lemmu, do your duty.
Arjuna said: O Sri Krishna, you have praised Karma Sanyasam (renunciation of works) and Karma Yoga (devotional work). Decide which of these two is better.
The Lord spoke: Both the path of Karma Sanyasa (renunciation of works) and the path of Karma Yoga (devout action) lead to the Supreme Goal. But Karma Yoga is superior to Karma Sanyasa.
Karma yogis who do not hate anything and do not expect anything should be known as eternal ascetics. Being beyond all dualities, they are gracefully liberated from material bonds.

Only the ignorant say that Sankhya (renunciation of karmas or karmic asceticism) and Karma Yoga (working with devotion) are different. Those who are truly knowledgeable say that one can get the fruits of both by adopting any one of these two paths.

The highest state attainable through karmic asceticism can also be attained by practicing karmas with devotion. Therefore, he who sees that Karma Sanyasama and Karma Yoga are one and the same has seen it as it really is.
It is very difficult to attain perfect karmic asceticism, O great-armed one, without performing bhakti yukta (karma yoga), but a sage skilled in karmic yoga quickly attains the supreme soul.
Karma yogis who have a pure inner self and control the sense-minds, see the Supreme Spirit of souls in every living being. They do not get caught up in karmabandhas while doing all kinds of work.

Those who are fixed in karma yoga - while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, moving, sleeping, breathing, speaking, excreting, taking in, opening and closing the eyes - always feel "I am not the doer". As the natural senses move in their respective objects, they are perceived by divine spiritual knowledge.

Those who are fixed in karma yoga - while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, moving, sleeping, breathing, speaking, excreting, taking in, opening and closing the eyes - always feel "I am not the doer". As the natural senses move in their respective objects, they are perceived by divine spiritual knowledge.
Those who renounce all material interests and dedicate all their deeds to the Lord, are untouched by sin, like a lotus is not wetted by water.
Yogis, abandoning mamakarasakti, practice karmas with body, mind, senses and mind only for soul purification.

Offering the fruits of all activities to the Lord, Karma Yogis attain eternal peace. At the same time, those who are motivated by their kama (desires) and act for selfish gain, become entangled in karmic bonds because they are interested in karmic fruits.
Soul-tempered and dispassionate living souls, knowing that they are neither the doer nor the cause of anything, are happy in this city of nine gates.
But the concept of karma, the nature of karma is not created by God. He is also not the creator of karmic fruits. It is the qualities of physical nature that actuate all these.
The Lord, who is omnipresent, does not partake of any sinful or pious deeds. Beings are deluded because their wisdom is covered by ignorance.
But, for those whose ignorance of the soul is destroyed by the divine spiritual knowledge, that knowledge illumines the Supreme Soul, as the sun illumines all in the day.

Those whose mind is fixed on God, who are fully engaged in God, who have firm faith that He is the ultimate goal - their sins are eradicated by the rays of knowledge, and attain a state of quick passing and no return.
True scholars, with the eyes of divine knowledge - see a Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog, a Chandal with equanimity.
Those who are fully minded in equanimity, conquer the cycle of birth and death in this very life. They possess the flawless qualities of God and thus attain the Supreme Truth.

Those who are established in God, have a firm understanding of divine spiritual knowledge and are free from delusion, do not get overwhelmed when the beloved happens/acquire, nor do they get depressed when anything unpleasant happens.
He who is not attached to external sense pleasures, enjoys divine bliss in the soul itself. Through yoga one gets united with God and experiences endless bliss.

The pleasures of sense materialism, though they may seem pleasurable to the worldly-minded, are actually causes of sorrow. O son of Kunti, such pleasures have an adi-antham (beginning-end), so the wise do not indulge in them.
Those who can control the forces of lust and anger before leaving this body are yogis and they alone are truly happy.

Whoever is happy (rejoicing) within themselves, enjoying the bliss of the Supreme Being within, and shining with the light of inner knowledge, such yogis, united with God, are freed from material worldly existence.

Those whose sins are destroyed, whose doubts are eradicated, whose minds are disciplined, who are engaged in the welfare of all living beings, such pious persons are freed from the material world and attain God.
Those ascetics who are freed from lust and anger, who have restrained the mind, who are in Atma-jnana through constant effort, are freed from material existence in these worlds.

Abandoning the thoughts of all external pleasures, focusing the attention between the eyes and the eyes, stopping the air entering and leaving the nostrils evenly, thus restraining the senses, mind and intellect, the sage who is free from lust, anger and fear dwells in the state of eternal salvation.

Abandoning the thoughts of all external pleasures, focusing the attention between the eyes and the eyes, stopping the air entering and leaving the nostrils evenly, thus restraining the senses, mind and intellect, the sage who is free from lust, anger and fear dwells in the state of eternal salvation.
Knowing that I am the bearer of all sacrifices and penances, the Lord of all worlds and the selfless friend of all living beings, Pidapa, my devotee will attain peace.

The Lord spoke: Those who perform kartavya karmas (duties to be performed) without any desire for fruit, are the true ascetics and yogis. Moreover, it is not only those who have stopped performing the Agni Hotra Yajna or those who have renounced physical activities.
Asceticism, as everyone thinks, is not different from Yoga. Because no one can become a yogi without renouncing worldly desires.
In yoga the striving (initial-stage) jivatama for perfection is called the means; For those who have reached a higher level in yoga, calmness is the tool of meditation.
When a person is disinterested in sense objects and karmas, that person is highly placed in the Yoga Shastra; Because he renounced all desires to enjoy the fruits of karma.
Lift yourself up by the power of your mind, but do not fall. Because mind can be our friend and mind can be our enemy.
For those who conquer the mind, it is their friend. For one who cannot do so, the mind acts as an enemy.
Yogis who have conquered the mind - cold, happy, sad, and angry - are above these dualities. Such Yogis are calm and have a fixed will in devotion to God.
Those who are satisfied with wisdom and discernment, conquerors of the senses, remain calm in all situations. They – clay, stones and gold – see them all with one eye.

Benefactors, friends, enemies, saints and sinners – yogis look with impartiality.  A yogi who is equanimous towards friends, associates and enemies, neutral towards enemies and relatives, and without partiality towards pious souls and sinners - is considered the best of all human beings.
Those who want to attain the state of yoga should be in meditation of Bhagavat with controlled mind-body, renouncing desires and pleasures, and in seclusion.
To practice yoga, prepare an asana in a clean place; It should be made of kusha grass, deer skin and a piece of cloth one over the other. This asana should neither be too high nor too low.

Sitting steadily on it, in single-minded meditation, restraining all thoughts and activities – the yogi must strive to purify his mind. He should keep his body, neck, and head firmly in the same order, and without turning his eyes to and fro, should concentrate his gaze on the nostrils.

Sitting steadily on it, in single-minded meditation, restraining all thoughts and activities – the yogi must strive to purify his mind. He should keep his body, neck, and head firmly in the same order, and without turning his eyes to and fro, should concentrate his gaze on the nostrils.
Thus, with calmness, fearlessness and stillness of mind and firm determination in the brahmacharya vrata, the mindful yogi should meditate on Me, the Supreme Goal.
In this way, the Yogi with a disciplined mind, constantly fixing his mind on Me, attains 'Nirvana' and abides in Me in supreme peace.
O Arjuna, whoever eats too much or eats too little; Those who sleep too much or sleep too little - they cannot succeed in yoga.
But he who is moderate in eating and amusements, balanced in work, and regular in sleep, can relieve all sorrows by the practice of yoga.
With perfect discipline, they turn the mind away from all selfish desires and fix the Lagna on the supreme welfare of the soul. Such are said to be in yoga, and they are beyond all sensual desires.
Just as a lamp stays still in a windless place, so the mind of a Yogi stays steady in the meditation of God.
When the mind is restrained from material activities and stilled by yoga practice, then the Yogi can see the Atman through a pure mind and revel in Atmanananda.
In that paramananda yogic state called samadhi, one experiences limitless divine bliss. A Yogi in this state never deviates from the Eternal Truth.
After attaining that status, Marinka feels that nothing is better than that. He who is thus established, is unmoved even in severe sorrows.
Yoga is the state of being freed from sorrows.  This yoga should be practiced with firm resolve without any pessimism/disbelief;

One should give up all desires arising from worldly thoughts and restrain the senses from all sides with the mind. Gradually and surely, with firm faith in Buddhi, the mind becomes fixed in God and thinks of nothing else.

One should give up all desires arising from worldly thoughts and restrain the senses from all sides with the mind. Gradually and surely, with firm faith in Buddhi, the mind becomes fixed in God and thinks of nothing else.
Whenever and wherever this fickle, unstable mind wanders, it should be brought back and constantly focused on God.
A Yogi who is calm in mind, calm in his passions, sinless, who sees everything in relation to Bhagavat – attains the highest transcendental bliss.
A self-restrained yogi unites the soul with God, attains freedom from material impurities, and attains the highest state of absolute bliss, always in union with the Supreme.
True yogis unite the inner mind with God and see all demons in God and God in all demons.
He who beholds Me in all, who beholds all in Me, will not miss Me, and I will not miss them.
The Yogi who is one with Me and worships Me as the Supreme Being who is present in all the demons, doing all kinds of activities, lives in Me.
I consider those who treat all beings equally and respond to the happiness and sorrows of others as if they were their own, as perfect yogis.
Arjuna said: O Madhusudana, this method of yoga that you mentioned, because of this restless mind, seems to me impracticable and impossible.
This mind is very restless, turbulent, strong and stubborn. Controlling it seems more difficult than controlling the wind, O Krishna.
Sri Krishna Paramatma said: O son of Kunti with great arms, you are right; The mind is indeed very difficult to control. But, it can be tamed by practice and dispassion.
Yoga is difficult for those who are not in control of the mind. But, those who learn to control the mind, and practice in the right way, can attain perfection in yoga. This is my opinion.

Arjuna said: What is the fate of the yogi who, even after starting this journey with diligence, due to a restless mind, does not exert enough effort and is unable to achieve the ultimate success of the goal of yoga in this life?
O great-armed Krishna, is not one who strays from the path of yoga depraved of both material and spiritual attainments? Is he like a cloud that is parted and scattered and becomes confused?
O Krishna, clear this doubt of mine completely, and who can do it better than you?
O Partha, he who is on the spiritual path will not perish either in this world or in the next world. Dear friend, one who strives for the attainment of Bhagwat will never suffer from Durga.

Those who are depraved of yoga (those who could not achieve success in yoga in this life), go to the holy worlds. Pidapa, who lived there for a long time, will be born back in the earth, in a family of pious and wealthy people. Or, those who have developed Vairagya due to long practice of yoga, will be born in a family of divine knowledge.  Such a birth is very rare.

Those who are depraved of yoga (those who could not achieve success in yoga in this life), go to the holy worlds. Pidapa, who lived there for a long time, will be born back in the earth, in a family of pious and wealthy people. Or, those who have developed Vairagya due to long practice of yoga, will be born in a family of divine knowledge.  Such a birth is very rare.
After taking such a birth, a Kuru vamsha, they reawaken the knowledge of their previous births and strive further for perfection in yoga.

They, though not of their own free will, are certainly drawn towards God by the instrumentality of previous births. Such sadhakas naturally rise above the principles of karma kandas enunciated in the Vedas.

With the merits acquired from many previous births, whenever these yogis mentally strive for further progress, they become purified (freed) from worldly desires and attain siddhi (perfection) in this very birth.
A yogi is superior to an ascetic, superior to a jnani, and even superior to a karmi. So, O Arjuna, try to become a Yogi.
Of all yogis, whose mind is always absorbed in Me, who is devoted to Me with firm faith, I regard them as supreme.
The Lord spoke: O Arjuna, if you can know Me completely, without doubt, by surrendering to Me through the practice of bhakti yoga, listen now.
Whatever knowledge and knowledge Pidapa has left to know nothing in this world, I will tell you completely.
Any one among thousands strives for perfect perfection; And only one of those who have attained perfect siddhi will truly know me.
Earth, water, fire, air, sky, mind, intellect and ego - these are the eight limbs of my physical Prakriti Shakti.

This is my low power. But, beyond that, O great-armed one, Arjuna, I have a superior power. That is the Jiva-Atma Shakti, which contains the Jiva-Atmans that are the basis of the living beings in this world.
Know that all living beings manifest through these two powers of mine. I am the origin of all this creation and in Me it all revolves.
There is nothing higher than me, O Arjuna. Everything depends on me like beads on a thread.
I am the taste of water, O son of Kunti, and I am the radiance of the sun and moon. In the Vedas I mean the sacred 'Om' Karam (pranava); A sound in the sky and their power in men.
I am the pure smell of the earth and I am the radiance in the fire. I am the life force in all beings, and I am the austerity in penances.
O Arjuna, know that I am the eternal seed of all beings. I am the wisdom among the wise, I am the brilliance among the bright.
I am the best of the Bharatas, the lustless strength of the mighty. Sexual acts that are not morally wrong.
The trigunas of material nature – sattva, rajas, tamas – are manifested by My energy. They are mine but I am beyond them.
Being deluded (bewitched) by the trigunas of Maya, the people of this world are unable to know Me, who is impermanent and eternal.
My divine power, 'maya', which is triune in nature, is very difficult to overcome. But, those who surrender to me can pass it gracefully.

Four kinds of men do not surrender to Me - those who lack knowledge, those who have the ability to know Me but lazily follow their lower nature, those who are deluded, and those who are endowed with asura power.

O best of Bharatas, four types of Dharma-parayanas engage in devotion to Me – those in distress, those who strive for the acquisition of knowledge, those who seek the acquisition of worldly goods, and those who are fixed on knowledge.
Of all these, those who worship Me with wisdom, and those who have firm resolve and exclusive devotion to Me, I regard as the best of all.  I am dear to them and they are dear to me.

All those who are devoted to Me are truly the best. But those who are wise, firm in determination, whose intellect is united in Me, and who have Me alone as their ultimate goal, I consider to be My very form.
After many births of spiritual practice, the wise one realizes that all that exists is Me (Vasudeva) and surrenders to Me. Such a Mahatma is very rare indeed.

Those who are lost in knowledge with material worldly desires surrender to other gods. They follow their own nature and worship other gods; Karma Kandas are performed to please the respective deities.
Whichever form of deity a devotee wants to worship with faith, I will make that devotee focus on that form.
A devotee who has sraddha faith worships that deity and gets the desired material. But, in fact, I am the one who provides those benefits.
But the fruit of these low-knowledge people is temporary. The worshipers of the deities go to the worlds of the respective deities, while My devotees reach Me.
The ignorant think that I, the Supreme Lord, Sri Krishna - who was once a formless immanence and has now assumed a form. They are unable to understand the literal, supreme form of this Self.
Covered by my Yogamaya Shakti, I do not manifest to all. So the ignorant cannot know that I am birthless and changeless.
Arjuna! I know all things past, present, and future, and all living things; But I don't know anyone.
O descendant of Bharata - Raga and hatred are dualities, arising from lust (delusion). O conqueror of enemies, every living being in this material world is deluded by these from birth itself.
Those whose sins are completely destroyed by performing pious activities are freed from the lust of these dualities. Such people worship Me with strong determination.
Those who take refuge in Me, striving to be freed from old age and death, realize Brahman, their own soul, and the field of all karma.
Enlightened living souls who know that I am the master of all adhibhuta (material realm), adhidaiva (gods), and adhiyajna (Lord of sacrifices), remain completely in Me even at the time of death.

Arjuna said: O Lord, what is Brahman (the Absolute Truth)? What is Adhyatma (Soul)? And what is karma? What is called adhibhuta? And who is called the supreme god? Who is Adhyajna in the body and how did he become Adhyajna? O Krishna, how is it possible for the strong-willed to know You at the time of death?

Arjuna said: O Lord, what is Brahman (the Absolute Truth)? What is Adhyatma (Soul)? And what is karma? What is called adhibhuta? And who is called the supreme god? Who is Adhyajna in the body and how did he become Adhyajna? O Krishna, how is it possible for the strong-willed to know You at the time of death?

Sri Bhagavan said: Brahman is the supreme, imperishable essence; The spirit of a person is called Adhyatma. Actions related to the material nature of living beings and their development are called karma or actions with fruition.

This ever-changing physical creation is called adibhuta; Adhidaiva is the cosmic form of God who is the head of the gods in creation; I, who reside in the hearts of all demons, am known as Adhiyajna, i.e. Lord of all Yajnas.
Remembering Me at the time of death he who leaves the body reaches Me. There is no doubt about this.
Whatever he remembers at the time of leaving the body at the time of death, O son of Kunti, always in the same meditation, he attains that state.
So, remember Me at all times and fight your duty. If your mind surrenders to Me, you will surely get Me; There is no doubt about this.
With practice, O Partha, if you constantly engage your mind in the remembrance of Me, the Supreme Lord, without wandering, you will surely attain Me.

God is omniscient, most ancient, all-ruling, subtler than the subtle, the basis of all, unimaginably divine; He is brighter than the sun and beyond all the darkness of ignorance.  He who, at the time of death, with the undisturbed mind acquired by the practice of yoga, keeping the soul between the eyes, calmly remembers the divine Mars with great devotion, will surely attain Him.

God is omniscient, most ancient, all-ruling, subtler than the subtle, the basis of all, unimaginably divine; He is brighter than the sun and beyond all the darkness of ignorance.  He who, at the time of death, with the undisturbed mind acquired by the practice of yoga, keeping the soul between the eyes, calmly remembers the divine Mars with great devotion, will surely attain Him.
Vedic scholars say that He is imperishable; To enter Him, great sages practice celibacy and renounce worldly pleasures. Now let me briefly explain the path to that goal.
Controlling all the portals of the body, stopping the mind in the heart position, drawing the prana into the Murdnya (head) position, one should remain in yogic meditation with concentration.
He who leaves the body, remembering Me, the Supreme Lord, chanting Om Kara, attains the Supreme Gati.
O Partha, I am easily accessible to the yogis who always remember Me with singleness of mind because they are constantly engaged in Me.
The Pidapa, the Mahatmas, who have attained me, have no rebirth in this world, the abode of sorrows and transitory, because they have attained the supreme perfection.
Throughout Brahmaloka, in all the worlds of this material creation, you will be reborn, O Arjuna. But Pidapa who has reached my abode, O son of Kunti, will never be reborn again.
A period of one thousand Chaturyugas (Mahayugas) would be one day (kalpa) for Lord Brahma and one night for him. The wise who understand this understand the reality of day and night.
As the dawn of Brahma begins, all beings arise from the immanent source. And as soon as His night begins, all living souls are absorbed into their manifest form.
As Brahma's day begins, all living beings begin to re-birth, and as Brahmaratri begins, they become re-arranged. And when the next Brahmapag begins, they all manifest effortlessly.
Apart from this manifest and immanent creation there is a transcendental and eternal immanent entity.  Even if all else perishes, that world alone is eternal and imperishable.
Its unmanifest expanse is the supreme goal, and after reaching it one does not return to this mundane (mortal) world. That is my passion.
The supreme Supreme Personality of Godhead is the Supreme. Although He is all-pervading and all living beings reside in Him, He is known only by devotion.

I will now explain to you, O best of Bharatas, the various ways of passing away from this world, one of which leads to salvation and the other to rebirth. Those who know the Supreme Brahman and leave this world during the six months of Uttarayana, in Shukla Paksha, during the day, attain Parama Pada. Those who practice Vedic Karma Kandala, during Dakshinayana six months, during Krishna Paksha, during Dhumra period, at night, leave this world - attain heavenly worlds. After experiencing the pleasures of heaven, they come back to this earth. These two - bright and dark, paths always exist in this world. The bright path leads to salvation and the dark path to rebirth.

I will now explain to you, O best of Bharatas, the various ways of passing away from this world, one of which leads to salvation and the other to rebirth. Those who know the Supreme Brahman and leave this world during the six months of Uttarayana, in Shukla Paksha, during the day, attain Parama Pada. Those who practice Vedic Karma Kandala, during Dakshinayana six months, during Krishna Paksha, during Dhumra period, at night, leave this world - attain heavenly worlds. After experiencing the pleasures of heaven, they come back to this earth. These two - bright and dark, paths always exist in this world. The bright path leads to salvation and the dark path to rebirth.
Yogis who know the secret of these two paths, O Partha, never fall prey to lust. Therefore, be sthitudavai (united with God) in yoga sarvada (at all times).
Yogis who know this secret - the practice of Vedic Karma Kandas, Vedadhyayana, performance of Yajnas, penance and charity - all these attain fruit beyond pious fruits. Such Yogis attain Parama Pada.

Sri Bhagavan said: O Arjuna, since you are not jealous of me, I will now tell you this most secret knowledge and empirical knowledge; After knowing this you will be freed from all material sufferings.
This knowledge is the king of all learning and the most secret. It sanctifies those who hear it. It is directly experiential, virtuous, easy to practice, and gives lasting results.
People who have no faith in this Dharma, cannot attain Me, O conqueror of enemies. They repeatedly return to this world in the cycle of birth and death.
This entire universe is pervaded by My inmanifest form. All beings abide in Me but I abide in them.
However, beings are not fixed in me. Behold the wonder of my divine power! Although I am the creator and administrator of all living beings, I am not affected by them or by material nature.
Even as the mighty wind that blows throughout, is always fixed in the sky, so all living beings are always fixed in Me.

At Kalpantara (at the end of a Kalpa), all beings merge into My primordial Prakriti Shakti. At the beginning of the next creation, O son of Kunti, I will manifest them again. Subduing my Prakriti (physical) energy, I am producing these innumerable living beings, according to their respective natures, again and again.

At Kalpantara (at the end of a Kalpa), all beings merge into My primordial Prakriti Shakti. At the beginning of the next creation, O son of Kunti, I will manifest them again. There are those who always remember Me and are engaged in exclusive devotion to Me, and to those whose mind is fixed on Me, I provide what they lack and preserve what they have.

I am equal-minded towards all living beings, I am neither partial nor hostile towards anyone. But, devotees who worship Me with love reside in Me and I reside in them.

Regardless of their birth, race, caste, gender, or even the society's abominations, all those who take refuge in Me attain the Supreme Word.
And what to say about the pious kings and ancestors? So, after entering this temporary and pleasureless world, engage in me with devotion.

Desire and hatred, happiness and sorrow, body, consciousness, mental force - all these together are called kshetra and its changes (vikaramula).

That which must be known, I will now tell you, after knowing it, one becomes immortal. That is the eternal Brahman which is beyond sat and asat.
Everywhere are His feet, eyes, heads and faces. His ears are also in all places, for He pervades the whole world.

Although He can know all sense objects, He is senseless. He is not attached to anything, yet He is the preserver and nurturer of all. Although He is Nirguna, He is the Bhokta of the trigunas of nature.
He is present both outside and inside all material demons. He is subtle, so we cannot understand Him. Far away but also very close.
He is indivisible, yet He is seen as different in all beings. Know that the Lord is the Sustainer-Sustainer, Sustainer and Creator of all bhutams (living beings).

He is the source of light among all luminaries, and the ultimate transcendence of the darkness of ignorance. He is knowledge, He is the object of knowledge, and He is the object of knowledge. He is in the hearts of all beings.

Thus I have explained to you the nature of the field, the meaning of knowledge, and the subject of knowledge. Only My devotees can truly understand this, and those who do so, they attain My divine nature.
Both Prakriti (physical nature) and Purusha (souls) are also anadiyana (sanatana). Know that all changes in the body and even the trigunas of nature are caused by material energy.
That physical energy is the cause of action in creation; It is said that Jivatma is responsible for experiencing pleasure and pain.
Whenever the Purusha (Jivatma) residing in Prakriti (physical energy) wants to enjoy the trigunas, it is Mamakarasakti for them, that Jivatma becomes the cause of high birth and low birth.
The Supreme Lord also resides in the body itself. He is said to be the All-Witness, the All-Appointer, the Sustainer, the Eternal Sustainer, the Supreme Authority and the Supreme Soul.
Those who understand the reality of the trinity of Paramatma, Jivatma, material nature and prakriti, will never be born here again. They will be liberated regardless of their current condition.

Some try to see the divine in their heart through meditation; And others seek to attain this through the acquisition of knowledge, and still others strive to attain this knowledge through the path of karma.

And some who are not aware of these spiritual paths, hear about them from others and start worshiping the Supreme Lord.  By listening to the Mahatmas with devotion like this, they too can gradually cross this ocean of birth and death.
O best of the Bharatas, know that you are all these living creatures, this field and the union of the Kshetrajna.
He who sees the Supreme Being in all living beings with their souls, and who sees both as impermanent in this transitory body, is truly seen.
Those who see that Lord, who is equal to all beings, the Supreme Soul, do not degrade themselves with their minds. Thus, they reach the Supreme Word.
It is the physical nature that does all the work (of the body) and the Jivatma actually does nothing - as one who understands has truly seen.
When they see that all beings with different qualities are situated in the same Prakriti, and understand that they are all emanated from the same, they attain knowledge of Brahman.

O son of Kunti, the Supreme Personality of Godhead is imperishable, eternal, without any physical attributes. Although present in the body, He does nothing, and is not at all tainted by material energy.

Akasa (empty space) contains everything within itself, but being subtle, is not tainted by what it contains. Similarly, although all its consciousness is pervaded in the body, the soul is not affected by the qualities of the body.
Just as one sun illuminates the entire solar system, so one soul illuminates the entire body (consciousness).
Those who observe the distinction of this ksetra and the ksetrajna with knowledge-eyes, and who know the method of liberation from material nature, attain the Supreme Padma.
Sri Bhagavan said: I will once again explain to you this supreme education, the best of all knowledge; Knowing this, all the great saints attained the highest perfection.
Those who take refuge in this knowledge will reach me. They are neither reborn at the time of creation nor destroyed at the time of Pralaya.

O great-armed Arjuna, the physical nature of energy consists of the three gunas – the sattva guna, the rajo guna, and the tamo guna. It is these qualities that bind the imperishable eternal soul to the perishable body.
Among these the sattva guna is holier than the rest, it is luminous and most salutary.  O sinless one, interest in knowledge and pleasure ensnares the soul.
O Arjuna, Rajo Guna is full of sensuality. It is born of worldly desires and affections and binds the soul with interest in lustful deeds.
O Arjuna, the tamo guna, born of ignorance, is the cause of the delusion of living souls.  It makes all living beings deluded by indifference, laziness and sleep.
Sattva binds one to material pleasures; Rajo guna makes the soul interested in karma; And tamo guna covers knowledge and binds one to delusion.
Sometimes Sattva has the upper hand over Rajotamas. Sometimes Rajo Guna dominates Sattva and Tamogunas; And some times Tamoguna overcomes Sattvarajo Gunas.

When all the portals of the body are illumined by knowledge, know that it is the manifestation of sattva guna. When Rajo guna prevails, O Arjuna, lobha (greed), industry for worldly gain, depression, and yava increase. O Arjuna – Ignorance, inertia, indifference, and lust – these are the main characteristics of Tamo Guna.

Sattva gives rise to knowledge, Rajo gives rise to greed (greed), and tamo gives rise to indifference and lust (delusion).
Those who are in sattva go to the upper worlds; Those who are in the Rajo Guna remain in the middle (of the worlds); Those who dwell in their own nature are degraded.
Whenever the wise know that in all actions, these tri-gunas are done and there is nothing else, and know that I am beyond these - they attain my divine nature.
By transcending the trigunas of physical nature, one is freed from the miseries of birth, death and old age and attains immortality.
Arjuna asked: What are the characteristics of one who is beyond the tri-gunas of nature, O Lord? How do they behave? How do they become beyond the bonds of tri-gunas?

Sri Bhagavan spoke: O Arjuna, those who are beyond these trigunas - neither hate (born in sattva guna) light, (born in rajo guna) activity, nor (born in tamo guna) delusion - when they are abundant, nor do they desire them when they are absent. They are neutral and indifferent to the qualities of nature and are not disturbed by them. Knowing that the gunas are acting, they remain still in the soul.

Sri Bhagavanu Palikenu: It is said about the Asvattha Vriksha which is an orthodox tree with roots upwards and branches downwards. Its leaves are Vedic mantras, and those who know the secret of this tree know the Vedas.

Nourished by the tri-gunas, the branches of this tree, extending up and down, sense objects are like gums to them. For karma to flow in human form, the roots of the tree are rooted downwards. Below, its roots spread out into branches, causing karma in the human world.

The real nature of this tree is not known in this world, nor is its beginning, end or orthodox existence understood. But, this deep-rooted tree of indifference must be cut down by the strong ax of apathy/vairagya. Then the beginning of that tree should be sought, that is God, from whom the production of this world took place long ago. After taking refuge in Him, we will not enter this world again.

Those who are free from avarice and lust, who have conquered lust, who are eternally in the mind of God, who have no desire to experience sensual pleasures, who are beyond pleasures, sorrows and dualities - such liberated beings attain my Parampada.
Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the fire can illuminate my supreme abode. People who went there never return to this physical world.
The living souls in the material world are the eternal aspects of Me. But, bound by physical energy, they are struggling with the six senses which are connected with the mind.
Just as the wind carries the fragrance from one place to another, so the soul, leaving the old body and entering the new body, takes the mind and senses along with it.
With the perception of the sense organs - ears, eyes, skin, tongue and nose - which are dependent on the mind, the living soul enjoys the sense objects.
Ignorant people do not notice the Jivatman - either when it is in the body enjoying sense objects or when it leaves the body. But those with wise eyes can see it.
Even the assiduous yogis are able to know the soul residing in the body. But, no matter how hard they try, those who are not purified in the inner world will not be able to know it.
Know that I am the effulgence of the sun that illuminates the entire solar system. Know that the radiance of the moon and the light of fire emanate from me.
Pervading and pervading the earth, I nourish all beings by My energy. Being the moon, I nourish all the plants.
I assume the form of Jatharagni, the soul-drinking soul in the stomachs of living beings, to digest and digest the four kinds of food.

I am present in the hearts of all beings, and from Me arise memory, knowledge, and forgetfulness. I am the only one to be known through all the Vedas, I am the author of Vedanta, and I am the knower of Vedardha.

There are two types of living beings in creation, Ksharams (perishable) and Aksharmas (imperishable). All that exists in the physical world is alkali. Aksharams are beings who have attained salvation.
Besides these, there is that Purushottam, the imperishable Supreme Soul. He enters the universe as the eternal God and sustains all living beings.
I am beyond this ephemeral material substance, and beyond the imperishable soul. Therefore I am glorified in the Vedas and Smritis as the Supreme Divine Man.
He who knows me without doubt as the Supreme Purushotta, has perfect knowledge. O Arjuna, they worship me wholeheartedly.
I have revealed to you, Arjuna, the most mysterious principle of Vedic science. One who understands this becomes wise, and accomplishes all that is to be attained.

Divine qualities lead to salvation, but demonic qualities cause one to remain trapped in bondage. Don't worry Arjuna, you were born with divine qualities.

There are two types of beings in this world - those with divine qualities and those with asura nature. I have elaborately described the divine qualities, O Arjuna, I will tell you about the nature of the Asuras, listen.
Those with asura qualities do not understand what is good conduct and what is bad conduct. That is why they are not chaste, or virtuous, or at least truthful.

They say, "There is no absolute truth in this world, no basis (of moral code), and no God (who created or maintains it). It all originates from male-female union and serves no other purpose than sexual gratification."  that
Firmly held in such a view, these misguided souls, with low intelligence and violent deeds, become enemies of the world and threaten to destroy it.

Filled with excessive lust, arrogance, avarice, pride and arrogance, these asura-characteristics hold false doctrines. Thus enamored, they are attracted to temporal things and act with an impure mind.
Their endless worry-worries ultimately end in death. However, they are convinced that the gratification of desires and the accumulation of wealth is the ultimate goal of life.
Bound by hundreds of desires, and beset by lustful wraths, they labor to amass wealth in unrighteous ways, all for the sake of their sensual pleasures.

There are three gates of hell that lead to the destruction of the soul - lust, anger, and greed. So, everyone should leave these.
Those who are freed from these three gates of darkness, strive for the well-being of the soul, so that they attain the ultimate goal.
Those who do not follow the instructions given in the Shastra, but are motivated by lust, they cannot achieve perfect Siddhi, happiness, and ultimately the ultimate goal of life.
So, let's take science as the standard of what to do and what not to do. Learn the rules and teachings of science and act accordingly in this world.
Arjuna said: O Krishna, what is the condition of those who renounce (neglect) the duties of science and yet worship with devotion? Is their faith in Sattva Guna or Rajo and Tamo Gunas?
Sri Bhagavan said: Every human being is born with his innate devotion/faith, which may be of three types - sattvik, rajas, or tamas. Now hear from me on this matter.
All men have beliefs according to the nature of their mind. Everyone has beliefs, and what they believe is their personality.
Those in sattva guna worship the gods; Those in Rajoguna worship Yakshas and Rakshasas; Those in the Tamo Guna worship ghosts.

Some people, driven by their vanity (hypocrisy) and pride, perform the most severe austerities, though unscientific.  Driven by lust and lust, they afflict not only their bodily organs but also Me, who is the Supreme Soul, within their bodies. Know that such mindless people are of asura nature.

People's food preferences depend on their nature.  Yajnas, penance, and charity also depend on their disposition. Now listen to these differences.
Virtue-dominant – likes things that increase longevity, and promote comfort, strength, health, happiness, and contentment. Such foods are juicy, nutritious, nutritious, and naturally delicious.
Foods that are very bitter, very sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry and spicy are preferred by those with Rajo guna predominance. Such foods cause suffering, grief and disease.
Dried/spoilt food, rotten food, contaminated and impure food – are dear to those who have Tamasi Guna as their predominance.
It is as if the yajna performed with sattva guna is performed with a firm determination in the mind that this is the duty to be done, following the rules of science without any desire for results.
O great Bharata, know that a yajna for worldly gain or pride is in Rajoguna.
A yajna performed without devotion and contrary to the rules of Shastra, without distribution of prasada, chanting of mantras, and without giving Dakshina, is considered to be of Tamo Guna.
Worship of the Supreme Lord, Brahmins, spiritual master, sages and elders - whenever it is done while practicing purity, chastity, celibacy and non-violence - is said to be physical penance.
Speech that does not cause emotion, truths, that does not cause anger, beloved things and recitation of eternal Vedic scriptures - these are said to be verbal penance.
Calmness of thought, gentleness, silence, self-restraint and purity of feeling - all these are known as penance of the mind.
If these three penances are practiced with great faith by the pious devotees without any expectation of material rewards, they are called sattvic penances.
For glory, honour, and magnanimity, ostentatious austerities/yagnas are in Rajo Guna. Its benefits are transient, and temporary.
Penance done with confused feelings, torturing oneself or harming others, is said to be in the nature of tamo.
Giving alms is said to be sattvaguna dana if one considers it a duty (right thing to do) and gives alms at the right time and in the right place, without any reward.
Donation given reluctantly, with the hope of something in return or with the expectation of a reward, is said to be in Rajo Guna.
Donation given at an inappropriate place, at an inappropriate time, to an undeserving (apatra), without courtesy, or carelessly, is considered tamasadana.
The words "Om Tat Sat" have been prescribed from the beginning of creation as indicative of Parabrahman. From them arose priests, sciences and yagnas.
So, in performing yajnas, in giving alms, in performing austerities - the Vedic vidus, following the Vedic injunctions, always begin by uttering the sound 'Om'.
Those who do not expect any counter-fruits, but seek to be freed from these material bonds, utter the word "tat" while performing penance, yajna, and charity.

The word "Sat" means - orthodox existence and auspiciousness. O Arjuna, it is also used to denote an auspicious action. The term "sat" also describes engaging in the practice of yajna, penance, and charity.  Therefore, any work with this purpose is called "Sat".
