Arjuna said: O great-armed Krishna, I want to know the nature of 'sannyasa' (renunciation of karma) and 'tyagama' (renunciation of the desire to enjoy the fruits of karma). O Hrishikesh, who desires to know the difference between them too, O Keshinishudana.
Sri Bhagavan said: Sanyasama, said the sages, is the renunciation of desires-induced karma. Pundits say that giving up all the fruits of karma is sacrifice.
Some learned men say that all forms of karma are sinful and should be avoided, while others say that yajna, charity and penance should never be given up.
Now listen to my final decision on the subject of sacrifice, O Purushavyagraha, it is said that sacrifice is of three types.
Karma related to yajna, almsgiving and austerities should never be renounced; They must be done. Indeed yajna, charity and penance sanctify even the wise.
These activities should be done without any desire for fruits and without any desire for reward. This is my absolute and supreme judgment, O Arjuna.
One should never renounce one's prescribed duties. Such confusion sacrifice is called Tamasika sacrifice.

Rajo Guna Tyaga is the act of abandoning one's obligatory duties, thinking that they are difficult or causing physical discomfort. Such a sacrifice is never salutary and does not contribute to our elevation.
Arjuna, whenever actions are performed in accordance with duty, and desire for fruit is renounced, it is called sattva guna sacrifice.
True sacrifices are those who do not try to avoid disliked tasks or wish for favorite/favorable tasks. They are virtuous and they have no doubts.
It is not possible for any living being with a body to renounce karma completely. Hence, one who renounces the fruits of his karma is said to be a true sacrificer.

For those who are interested in self-interest, even the deceased Pidapa, - happiness, sorrow and a mixture of the two - will have karmic rewards in these three forms.  But, those who perform karmaphala sacrifice will not have such fruits either in this world or in the next world.
O Arjuna, listen now to what Samkhya Shastra says about the five factors behind any action, which explains how to prevent karmic reactions.
Body, Karta, various senses, various kinds of effort, divine grace - these are the five limbs of karma.

Whatever karma/deed done by the body, speech, mind, be it good or bad, these five are its factors. Those who do not understand this think that the soul is the real doer. Such people with impure mind cannot understand the reality.

Abandoning the sense of kartrutva ahamkara bhava (the sense that I am the doer) and whose intellect is disinterested, even if they kill living beings, they are not killed and become bound by karma.
Jnana, Jnya (the object of knowledge), and the seeker of Jnana - these three induce Karma. Karana, Kriya, Karta, - these are the three limbs of Karma.
Sankhya Shastra states that these are three types of tri-gunas of nature - knowledge, karma, and action. Listen as I tell you these differences now.
The knowledge in sattva guna is knowing that there is one undivided, impermanent entity in all the different forms of life.
Realize that any knowledge which sees the different kinds of beings in different bodies as separate and unrelated to each other is rajasika (in rajaguna).

In the case that the entire creation is made up of these different parts, it is said that the knowledge that makes man completely alien to himself, without logic and far from truth, is tamasic knowledge.
That which is done according to karma-sastra, is free from lust, and is done without desire for fruit, is said to be in sattva guna.
Work motivated by selfish desire, carried out by pride, and involving intense effort is said to be in Rajoguna.
Karma that one does, starting from delusion, without knowing what one's self-power is, and without thinking about the consequences, loss and harm to others - is called Tamasika Karma.
Those who are free from ego and association, and have enthusiasm, determination, and are indifferent to success or failure are said to be virtuous doers.
A Karta who is interested in the fruits of karma, greedy, violent-inclined, impure, and affected by Harsha-Sokamas is considered to be in Rajoguna.
Those who are undisciplined, scornful, foolish, foolish, mean, lazy, desperate and carelessly waste time - may be called tamoguna kartas.
Now listen, O Arjuna, I will explain at length the difference between the intellect and the senses according to the trigunas of nature.

O Partha, what is the right deed, what is the bad deed;  What is duty, what is not duty; What to fear, what not to fear; Buddhi is said to be in Sattva Guna when it is understood what is binding and what is salvation.
Whenever the mind is confused as to what is right and what is wrong, when it cannot know what is right behavior and what is wrong, then that mind is in Rajoguna.
Tamoguna Buddhi is the mind which is enveloped in darkness and considers unrighteousness as righteousness and falsehood as truth.
Strong will developed through yoga; And the will that underlies the activities of the mind, prana vayus, and senses is called sattva guna dhrdhamsakata.
Rajasika dhruthi is a fixed mind motivated by desire and interested in dharma (duties), kama (pleasures) and artha (wealth).
Tamoguna dhruthi is the low minded will that is unrelenting, daydreaming, fearful, grieving, depressed and arrogant.
And now hear from me, O Arjuna, about the three kinds of pleasures which the living soul attains, and about the attainment of the stage of liberation from all sorrows.
Sattva guna happiness is happiness that seems like poison in the beginning, but in the end is like nectar. It is born of the pure intellect that is rooted in self-knowledge.
The pleasure due to the contact of sense objects with the senses is called rajasic (rajo guna) pleasure. This pleasure is like nectar in the beginning, but in the end it is like poison.
Whatever happiness - covering the entire existence of the soul from beginning to end, and arising from sleep, laziness, and carelessness - is said to be tamasic (in tamoguna) happiness.
In this physical world - not on earth, or in the upper heavenly worlds - not a single living being is beyond the influence of these trigunas of nature.
Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras – whose duties were assigned according to their characteristics, their respective qualities. (not in terms of birth).
Sama (tranquility), dama (sensual restraint), austerity, purity, patience, sincerity, wisdom, knowledge, and faith in this world – these are the innate karmic qualities of Brahmins.
Valor, strength, courage, skill in arms training, determination not to back down from battle, large-hearted kindness, and leadership ability - these are the karmic qualities inherent in Kshatriyas.
Agriculture, dairy farming, and trade are natural occupations for those with Vaishya Gunas. Serving by performing deeds is the natural duty of those with shudra qualities.
By performing the duties of those who are naturally born, human beings can attain perfect siddhi. Now hear from me how one can achieve perfection by practicing/performing his assigned duties.
By performing his natural occupation one worships Him - from whom all the demons sprang and by whom the whole world is filled and concentrated.  By doing such things one attains Siddhi easily.
It is better for a person to do his own self-righteousness, even if it is not done properly, than to do para (others') dharma. In performing the duties of his nature, man does not incur sin.

One should never forsake the duties born of one's natural nature, even if there are faults in them, O son of Kunti. All karmic efforts are shrouded in some kind of dosha, just as a fire is shrouded in smoke.
Whose intellect is dispassionate throughout, who conquers the mind and renounces desires through the practice of asceticism, attains the supreme Naishkarmya Siddhi.
O Arjuna, how one who has attained perfect siddhi (in karmic asceticism) can attain Brahman also by being established in transcendental spiritual knowledge - hear me in brief.

Such a person likes solitude, eats in moderation, controls body language, engages in constant meditation and practices dispassion. A person who is free from ego, violence, avarice, desires, selfishness, selfishness - is peaceful and deserves to attain the state of oneness with the Supreme Being. A person who is at one with Parabrahman is mentally calm, does not grieve for anything, does not desire for anything. Being equanimous towards all beings, such a yogi will receive my parabhakti.
Only through loving devotion to Me can I know who (how much) I really am. Knowing Me, Pidapa, My devotee is absorbed in My absolute consciousness.
My devotees take full refuge in Me even though they are doing all the activities. By my grace they will attain eternal and impermanent abode.
Make me your supreme goal and offer your every karma to me. Take refuge in Buddhi Yoga and make your will always ascend to me.
If you always remember Me, by My grace you can overcome all obstacles and difficulties. But if, through pride, you do not listen to my advice, you will perish.
If you are motivated by pride and think, "I will not fight," then your decision will be wasted anyway. Because it is your own (Kshatriya) physical nature that impels you to fight.
O Arjuna, whatever action you say you will not do due to lust, you will be prompted to do it by the impulse born of your natural nature.
Ishvara resides in the heart of all beings, O Arjuna. He directs the course of the living souls who ascend the Yantra made of material energy, according to their respective karmas.
Surrender completely to Him alone, O Bharata.  By His grace, you will attain supreme peace and eternal abode.
Thus I have revealed to you the most secret knowledge of all secrets. Think deeply about it, and do as you like.
Hear once again My supreme instruction, which is the most secret of all knowledge. I am telling you this for your sake, because you are very dear to me.
Always remember Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me and bow to Me. By doing this you will surely reach me. This is my promise to you, because you are very dear to me.
Abandon all kinds of dharmas and surrender to Me alone. I will absolve you of all sins, fear not.
This Upadesha should never be given to a non-ascetic, a non-pious person. (Spiritual matters) Do not say this even to those who are averse to hearing, and especially to those who are envious of me.
Whoever inculcates this supremely secret knowledge among My devotees, they have performed supreme loving service. They will undoubtedly reach me.
No one has done me more loving service than they; There will be no one on this earth dearer to me than they.
Those who recite this holy dialogue between us, worship Me with the sacrifice of knowledge (with their intellects); That is my opinion.
Even those who merely hear this knowledge, with earnest faith and without envy, are freed from sins and reach the holy worlds where the pious souls reside.
O Arjuna, did you listen attentively to what I said? Are your ignorance and delusion eradicated?
Arjuna said: O Achyuta (blameless one), by your grace my delusion is eradicated, and I am established in knowledge. I have no doubts now, and will do according to your instructions.
Sanjay said: Thus, I, heard the conversation between Lord Krishna, son of Vasudeva, and Arjuna, son of Mahatma, Pritha. It's so amazing it makes my hair stand on end.
By the grace of Vedavyasa, I learned this supreme secret of yoga from Lord Krishna himself.
I am rejoicing over and over again recalling this magnificent conversation between the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna and Arjuna.
And, remembering the wonderful and astonishing cosmic form of Sri Krishna, I am amazed and thrilled with great joy again and again.
It is my firm opinion that wherever Sri Krishna, the Yogeshwar, and Arjuna, the supreme archer, are there, there is all wealth, all victory, all-plenty and righteousness.
